title: Diagram Scene Protocol Scene Schema
description: Draft JSON Schema for the canonical DSP scene document. Licensed under Apache-2.0; the spec and both schemas are at https://github.com/zindexai/diagram-scene-protocol.

extensions.description: Reserved extension point for protocol additions. Recognized keys include `showLifelineFeet` and `autonumber` (sequence diagrams only) and `autoGroup` (architecture diagrams and diagrams without a family). updateScene sets these keys and `layoutHints`, and no others.

showLifelineFeet.description: Sequence-diagram only. When true (default), the renderer draws a foot bar at the bottom of each lifeline mirroring the head (UML / PlantUML / Mermaid convention). Set to false to suppress foot bars - useful when the author authors their own bottom row of shapes.

autonumber.description: Sequence diagrams only: numbers every drawn message, top to bottom, each time the diagram is drawn, with a numbered badge at the start of its arrow. true counts from 1 by 1; an object sets where the count starts (start) and what it goes up by (increment), each a whole number from 1 and 1 when left out. A message's own step is drawn as given and the count goes on from it, as Mermaid's autonumber with a number restarts it partway down. Notes, hidden messages and messages to or from a hidden lifeline take no number, and the count skips them. Numbers are whole numbers: write numbering such as 1.1 in the label instead. In every other family it draws nothing (AUTONUMBER_NOT_DRAWN): give the edges you want numbered a step.

start.description: The first message's number; 1 when left out.

increment.description: What each next message's number goes up by; 1 when left out.

autoGroup.description: Architecture diagrams and diagrams without a family only. When set, the engine synthesizes subtle background bands grouping nodes by their `nodeType` (e.g. one band for all `service` nodes, one for `database` nodes, one for `externalSystem` nodes). Each band is labeled with the pluralized type name ("Services", "Databases", "External Systems"). Skipped when the scene already authors frames containing the candidate nodes (no double-wrap), when all nodes share a single `nodeType` (trivial), or when the nodes of a type are scattered (a node of another type sits between two of them in a column) or placed so that their band would overlap a frame or another band. Opt-in only; omit the field to render with no banding (existing default).

diagramFamily.description: Diagram family declaration. Technically optional in the schema but effectively load-bearing: gates family-specific validation, layout, and rendering behavior the engine and downstream tooling rely on (sequence-family fan-in exemption, ER auto-promote-fk-labels, workflow BPMN conventions, family-namespaced node types). Without it the diagram is drawn as an architecture diagram, and nothing warns you. Always declare on every scene.

layoutStrategy.description: How the engine places the nodes that have no position. The engine picks its placement method from diagramFamily: a layered layout for architecture, flowchart, workflow, entityRelationship and uiflow diagrams and for diagrams without a family, which read these fields; a tree for orgchart (top to bottom), forces for network, and message order for sequence, which don't. A field left out takes the layered layout's default.

direction.description: Layout direction: top to bottom, bottom to top, left to right, right to left. The default is LR, and TB for flowchart and orgchart.

nodeSpacing.description: Pixels the engine aims for between nodes in the same rank. Not a minimum: when it lays out every node it also tries tighter and wider spacings and keeps the layout that scores best, and it widens gaps to fill a larger canvas.

rankSpacing.description: Pixels the engine aims for between adjacent ranks: 80 by default, 50 in a flowchart. Not a minimum: when it lays out every node it also tries tighter and wider spacings and keeps the layout that scores best, and it widens gaps to fill a larger canvas.

palette.description: Scene-level color palette that overrides theme defaults for unstyled elements. All properties optional - only specify the colors you want to override. Cascade: element style > palette > theme > fallback.

accentPrimary.description: Accent color of nodes whose style sets no accentColor: ER table headers and PK badges, org chart card stripes, UI flow screen and modal title bars

accentSecondary.description: Nothing draws a second accent yet, so this has no effect

color.description: CSS-compatible color string. Implementations may choose to restrict this further.

metadata.description: Freeform metadata for provenance or custom annotations.

rotation.description: Kept with the layout. The reference engine doesn't rotate anything.

units.description: The units of every position and size. Only px.

id.description: The diagram's ID. Zindex sets it when the diagram is created through /v1/diagrams or diagram_create, ignoring any value sent.

brief.description: Context kept with the diagram for the next agent: what it shows, conventions to keep, decisions made. Versioned with the diagram.

lang.description: The language the diagram's text is in, a BCP 47 language tag such as `ja`, `ko`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant` or `zh-HK`. When it names Chinese, Japanese or Korean, it picks the letterforms of Chinese characters. Without it, or with another language, the forms are inferred from the text: kana is Japanese, Hangul is Korean, and other Chinese characters are Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese or Japanese by the forms they use. A diagram whose Chinese characters Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese all share is read as Simplified Chinese. Japanese written without kana can read as Traditional Chinese. Set `lang` when you know the language. Hong Kong forms need `zh-HK`. A tag that isn't well formed is an error (`LANG_INVALID`).

extensions.description: Not kept: the reference engine drops it when it stores the diagram. Put data in the document's top-level extensions instead.

grid.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine draws no grid.

snap.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine doesn't snap to a grid.

viewport.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine doesn't read it.

sceneDefaults.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine doesn't read these: set fonts, strokes and routers on elements or in styles.

fontFamily.description: Never drawn from: set `fontFamily` on elements or in styles. Any value but `sans` returns the warning `FONT_FAMILY_UNKNOWN`, `mono` too.

zIndex.description: Paint order: higher draws on top. When absent, the engine assigns one by kind, counting up in array order within each kind: frames from 0, groups from 100, edges from 200, nodes from 300, text from 400, images from 500 and guides from 600.

locked.description: Kept with the element. The reference engine edits and draws an element whatever its value.

visible.description: false hides the element: the engine still lays it out, so it keeps its space, but doesn't draw it or any edge with an end at it. A hidden frame hides only its box and title, and a hidden group (which draws nothing) drops only its SVG `<title>`; their members stay drawn.

oneOf.description: Reference to a named style in scene.styles

style.description: Element style: either a named-style string key (resolved against scene.styles) or an inline StyleValue object

columns.description: ER table columns, read by er.entity and er.weakEntity nodes. Each column draws as a row; an edge anchors at a row with endpoint.column, and an edge end left without cardinality is inferred from the column's flags. updateNode replaces the whole array.

operator.description: A sequence fragment's operator (a frame whose containerType is fragment): alt, opt, loop, par, break, critical, neg or ref, drawn in its tab as written.

operands.description: A sequence fragment's operands after its first, top to bottom. Each starts at one of the fragment's rows (startsAt, a message or note id, after its first row) and may carry a guard; a dashed divider is drawn above that row, for every operator, with the guard under it in brackets the renderer adds. The first operand is the fragment's own, with the frame's title, drawn as written, as its guard. An operand with a y is refused; a version stored with one still draws, each such operand at the first message or note drawn at or past its y.

startsAt.description: A sequence.activation's first message: the bar starts at that message's arrow, on the lifeline it arrives at.

endsAt.description: A sequence.activation's last message: the bar ends at that message's arrow. Without it, the bar is as tall as one row at startsAt.

anchor.description: A sequence.note's place: the ID of the participant it sits over, or an array of two or more IDs it spans, from the leftmost to the rightmost. A note without an anchor that names a participant isn't drawn.

side.description: A sequence.note with one anchor: drawn beside that lifeline, on its left or right, instead of over it. Ignored on a note across lifelines (an array anchor), which is always drawn over them (FAMILY_SEQ_NOTE_SIDE_IGNORED).

x.description: Shorthand for layout.x - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

y.description: Shorthand for layout.y - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

width.description: Shorthand for layout.width - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

height.description: Shorthand for layout.height - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

startsAt.description: The row the operand starts at: a message or note inside the fragment, after its first row.

guard.description: The operand's guard, drawn in brackets after its divider.

erColumn.description: One column of an ER table (er.entity, er.weakEntity): drawn as a row with its PK/FK badges and type.

name.description: Column name, drawn on its row. endpoint.column, and an edge label that names a foreign key, match it.

type.description: Column type, drawn right-aligned on the row.

pk.description: Part of the primary key. An edge end at the only PK column infers one; at one of several, many.

fk.description: A foreign key. An edge end here infers many: one when unique (or the entity's only PK column), zero-or-many when nullable, zero-or-one when both.

unique.description: Unique on its own: a unique foreign key infers one.

nullable.description: Nullable: a nullable foreign key infers zero-or-many, or zero-or-one when unique.

key.description: Alias for pk: true or fk: true. A column that is both needs pk and fk.

comment.description: Kept with the column (a Mermaid attribute comment), not drawn.

autoSize.description: 'content' sizes a node whose label wraps (textStyle.wrap 'word' or 'character') to its text: it keeps this width and gets at least the height its wrapped label and icon need, the height a TEXT_OVERFLOW warning gives, growing down from its top edge. The height here is the minimum. Nodes it grows into move down to make room, keeping the full spacing from it: the node spacing in a left-to-right flow, the rank spacing (layoutStrategy.rankSpacing) in a top-to-bottom one. No effect on a label set to 'auto' or 'none' (the engine already sizes that node to it) or on nodes that lay out their own text: org chart people and roles, UI flow screens and modals, ER tables with columns, sequence nodes, BPMN events and gateways, UI flow entry and exit points.

layout.description: Position and size. Leave it out and the engine places the node next to its neighbors, around the nodes that have a layout, and sizes it to its content. After the first save the engine records the position here and keeps it, unless a node that grows needs the room and pushes this one, a node an edit adds needs more room for its edge label than the column it joins and this node is in that column or beyond it, a task an edit adds to a lane grows the lane and this node lies past the lane, a task an edit inserts between two placed columns of a pool opens a column and this node is in that column or beyond it, a node an edit inserts in a flowchart, between two placed nodes, needs room and this node lies past it, an AWS diagram's row or column grows (for a node or a spanning frame's header an edit adds, or for the room round a tier frame) or an edit moves its Region's column right to keep a labeled line into the column clear, and this node lies past the growth, an edit moves this node to another lane (it is placed again there), an edit adds or deletes a frame around it and keeping it would leave frames overlapping or a frame holding a node that isn't its member, or an added order constraint finds its two nodes the wrong way around; the autoLayout op, and a new or removed layoutStrategy or diagramFamily, place nodes again. Sequence diagrams are laid out from their messages, so their nodes stay at x 0, y 0. A layout at exactly x 0, y 0 counts as not placed.

icon.description: Icon key ({family}:{id}, e.g. lucide:database), or an image as a `data:` URI (a URL stays a link most viewers don't load)

router.description: How the edge is drawn. `orthogonal`, the default when `router` is left off (and `polyline`, drawn the same), is right-angle segments the engine routes round other nodes where a route exists. `straight` is one line between the two nodes' centers, ending where it crosses each node's outline. `curved` is one bowed arc between the two nodes, ending on each outline; a lone curve bows to the side that clears other nodes where one does, and curves between one pair of nodes spread into a lens. Neither `straight` nor `curved` is routed round nodes: one that runs through a node gets the warning EDGE_CROSSES_NODE. Sequence messages ignore `router`.

anchor.description: Where this end of the edge meets its node: `side` alone fixes the side, and the end sits where the engine spreads ends on that side; with `offset` it sits at that place, 0 to 1 from the top of a left or right side or the left of a top or bottom side, with the same corner distance as any end (8 px, more past a rounded corner). An anchored edge joins no shared trunk. The engine doesn't move nodes for it, so an anchor on the side facing away from the other node routes round the node. Ignored, with EDGE_ANCHOR_IGNORED, on a sequence message, a self-loop, or an end that names a column.

side.description: The side of the node this end meets.

offset.description: Where on the side, 0 to 1 from its top (left and right sides) or its left (top and bottom sides). Omit it to let the engine place the end on the side.

endpoint.description: Edge endpoint. elementId may reference any element kind - typically a node, but frame and group IDs are also valid targets. An edge to a frame terminates at the frame's border, on the side facing the source, straight across where the source lines up and otherwise at the side's center; useful for abstract group dependencies (e.g. an edge to a 'Regional Services' sidebar rather than to a specific service inside). On entityRelationship diagrams, set `column` to anchor the edge at a specific column row inside the entity (matching the dbdiagram.io / DBeaver convention where FK edges point at the FK column itself rather than the entity rectangle as a whole).

column.description: Optional column-row anchor for ER entities. When set, must match the `name` of a column declared in the endpoint entity's `extensions.columns` array. The edge's segment touching this endpoint anchors at the column row inside the entity instead of the entity's outer face. Mismatched names emit an EDGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND warning.

cardinality.description: ER-style cardinality marker for this endpoint. Omitted, it is inferred from the column the end anchors at each time the diagram is drawn, and isn't stored, so it follows the column.

edgeEndpoints.description: Arrowheads at each end. An arrowhead left out comes from the edge's edgeType: workflow.messageFlow has an open circle at the source and an open triangle at the target, sequence.async and sequence.reply an open triangle at the target, and every other type, default included, a filled triangle at the target and none at the source. In a diagram with an aws.* group frame or a node with an aws: icon, an edge whose edgeType is unset, default, or an er.*, network.* or org.* type draws AWS's open arrow, openTriangle, at the target instead; workflow.sequenceFlow, sequence.message, sequence.create, sequence.destroy and the uiflow.* types keep the filled triangle there.

label.description: Edge label text. Plain strings render as a single tspan. Labels matching the state-machine / SCXML / BPMN convention 'EVENT [guard] / action' render with multi-tier typography: event 12px, guard 10px muted, action 10px muted italic. Detection is content-based (balanced [...] OR ' / ' separator), in flowchart, workflow, uiflow and sequence diagrams; in every other diagram, one with no diagramFamily included, a label is plain text. Multi-line labels (containing \n) skip the convention parse.

waypoints.description: Kept with the edge, but not drawn: the engine routes every edge itself and doesn't pass through these points.

edgeType.description: Family-specific edge type for typed connection semantics

step.description: A numbered step: a badge with this number beside the start of the line, as AWS's architecture diagrams number a request's path, and at the start of a sequence message's arrow, as Mermaid numbers messages. Drawn in every family, never for a hidden edge. Edges may share a number; those with one number and one source share a badge. The engine draws the numbers given and numbers no other edge, except in a sequence diagram whose document sets extensions.autonumber, which numbers every message and counts on from a message's step. Whole numbers only: write numbering such as 1.1 in the label instead.

stepText.description: This edge's line in the step list drawn right of the diagram: steps in number order, each edge's text under its step's badge. Needs step, and is held to the label's length limit. A step whose edges have no stepText has no entry; with no stepText at all there is no list.

title.description: Not drawn: written into the SVG as the group's `<title>`. For a visible titled box, use a frame.

icon.description: An icon in the frame's header: a family:id key, or an image as a `data:` URI (a URL stays a link most viewers don't load). An AWS key draws as AWS draws a group icon, a 35 px square flush in the frame's top-left corner with the title beside it (and a frame with an AWS service icon and no stroke takes the service's category color, solid: AWS's custom group); any other icon draws 16 px before the title in the title's color. It replaces an aws.* preset's own icon.

spans.description: Makes this a spanning frame: drawn round these nodes and frames (an Auto Scaling group across Availability Zones), outside the containment tree. It holds nothing (no children), no frame or group lists it, its layout is ignored, and it spans no other spanning frame. Each target keeps its own frame. Drawn in architecture diagrams and diagrams without a family (SPAN_NOT_DRAWN elsewhere), round the union of its targets with no fill; an AWS diagram's rows keep room for its header. Its box is one rectangle, so a node inside it that it doesn't span gets SPAN_COVERS_NODE.

layout.description: A frame's box. Ignored in a sequence diagram, where a fragment or highlight band is laid out with its rows and a participant box with its lifelines.

containerType.description: What the frame stands for; generic when absent. pool and lane are BPMN's swimlanes, which the engine lays out itself: a pool's children are its lanes (frames with containerType lane), in the order they stack, and a lane's children are its tasks, events and gateways, or lanes of its own. Lanes run along the flow and stack across it, every node a lane lists is placed inside it, each lane is as deep as its contents need, and columns are shared across lanes and pools. Leave layout off pools, lanes and their nodes: a pool's or lane's layout is a minimum, not a fixed box, and a lane's x and y are ignored. fragment is a sequence diagram's combined fragment, laid out with its rows. Any other frame in a sequence diagram is drawn by its children: a participant box round lifelines, or a highlight band behind messages and notes; one that holds both isn't drawn, and boxes don't nest or overlap. The aws.* types are AWS's groups (AWS Architecture Icons): aws.cloud, aws.region, aws.vpc, aws.az, aws.subnet.public, aws.subnet.private, aws.securityGroup, aws.autoScalingGroup, aws.account and aws.corporateDataCenter, each drawn in AWS's color, line and corner icon with no fill and its title in the node label's size, nested as AWS nests them (AWS Cloud, Region, VPC, Availability Zone, subnets); style overrides the preset. In an architecture diagram, or one without a family, aws.cloud, aws.region, aws.vpc, aws.az and the two subnet types also place what they hold as AWS's reference diagrams do (Availability Zones as columns, subnets as rows across them, gateways on the side of the VPC they face, or on its top when they serve several AZs or the load balancer between two, regional services beside the VPCs, global ones above the Regions): leave layout off them and their nodes, a preset's layout being only a minimum, and nest them directly: a generic frame round whole VPCs of a Region, round all of a VPC's Availability Zones, or round subnets next to each other in one zone's rows (a tier), is read through, but any other frame between a Region and its VPC, or a VPC and its Availability Zones, is laid out as any frame with the presets inside it, and one between a zone and its subnets puts everything in it on one row after the zone's subnets; a generic one there gets the warning AWS_FRAME_HIDES_GROUPS. A security group or Auto Scaling group across Availability Zones is a spanning frame: give it spans instead of children. The other aws.* types only draw (an aws.account holding Regions is arranged as aws.cloud is). The other types draw as a generic frame does.

laneDirection.description: On a pool: how its lanes stack. Lanes always run along the flow and stack across it. vertical stacks them top to bottom, which BPMN calls a horizontal pool, and the flow runs left to right (LR, or RL when layoutStrategy.direction asks for it). horizontal puts them side by side, a vertical pool, and the flow runs top to bottom (TB, or BT). When layoutStrategy.direction runs along the lanes' stacking, laneDirection wins and the flow turns. Without laneDirection, lanes stack across the scene's direction: top to bottom in a left-to-right flow (the default outside flowcharts and org charts), side by side in a top-to-bottom one. The first pool in document order with a laneDirection sets the flow for the whole diagram. Lanes along the flow (phases) aren't supported.

wrap.description: 'auto', a node's default, keeps the label on one line while its node can grow to hold it, up to 250 px of content (wider if the layout gives more); a longer label wraps there and the node grows taller. On a text element, 'auto' wraps when the text is wider than its box. 'none', a text element's default, breaks lines only at \n, and a node grows as wide as the line. 'word' wraps to fit the width, and a word wider than the width runs past it. 'character' also breaks such a word between its characters. Wrapped text breaks by the Unicode line breaking rules (UAX #14), with Korean kept whole between spaces: at spaces, after hyphens and slashes, and between Chinese or Japanese characters. Only 'character' breaks inside a word, number or date, and only one wider than the width.

align.description: Horizontal alignment. When absent: center on a node, left on a text element.

verticalAlign.description: Vertical alignment. When absent: middle on a node, top on a text element.

fontFamily.description: `sans` (Inter, the default) or `mono`, a monospace font for paths, endpoints and types. Any other value draws in the default font and returns the warning `FONT_FAMILY_UNKNOWN`.

dash.description: Dash pattern, as SVG stroke-dasharray. On a frame drawn the generic way (generic, boundary, package, partition, subprocess and the aws.* presets): left out, a generic frame is dashed 4,4 and a preset takes its own; [] draws solid. Pools, lanes and fragments keep their own drawing.

accentColor.description: Accent color: the header and PK badges of an ER table, the stripe of an org chart card, the title bar of a UI flow screen or modal

color.description: Alias for textColor (normalized to textColor at runtime)

forceLabel.description: Edge-only: draw the edge's label where the engine would leave it out. When an edge's label exactly matches the name of a column declared in either endpoint's extensions.columns, the edge anchors at that column's row inside the entity (the dbdiagram.io / DBeaver convention) and the label isn't drawn, because the row carries the FK identity. Set this to true to draw the label as well: the edge still anchors at the column, and its cardinality at that end is inferred from the column.

id.description: Optional. Unique among the document's constraints when given: removeConstraint removes a constraint by its id.

columns.description: Elements per row; the elements fill as many rows as they need.

elements.description: Each element is centered in the container on both axes.

computed.description: The drawing output an implementation works out: element boxes, edge routes, label positions and the layout's diagnostics. Output, not input: any value passes. The reference engine ignores it, works it out again each time it lays the document out, and leaves it out of the documents it returns.
